art_instructions: A cozy attic bedroom with creamy walls, exposed wooden beams, and soft amber lamplight from a small lantern on a nightstand sets the scene. Along the far wall beneath the sloped ceiling are four small rich-brown wooden beds with rounded corners and forest-green blankets: from left to right, Panda, Koala, and Dinosaur sleep soundly while Owl is awake on the rightmost bed. Panda lies on his back with the blanket to his chest, mouth slightly open; Koala is curled on his side hugging a small pillow; Dinosaur, a friendly green child with rounded back-spikes, sleeps with the tip of his tail peeking from under the blanket. Owl sits upright on top of his covers, eyes wide and bright, head turned toward the door, wings slightly lifted in alert curiosity. On the left edge of the room, a wooden door stands just ajar, as if pushed open a moment ago. Suddenly, at least thirty tiny gray and brown mice (about the size of Owl’s foot) pour in under and around the door in a loose stream, fanning out across the soft rug; a few have already reached the middle of the room, and one climbs the leg of a low toy shelf. The mice look cute and non-threatening, with shiny eyes and whiskers, and none are being chased or eaten yet. The high-angle wide view should show the warm lamplight, green blankets, rugs, shelves of stuffed animals, and the flowing crowd of mice without waking the sleeping friends.
